READABILITY.evidence: Names mostly explain themselves (updateAfterSalePreview, refundedBySku, remainingPayable, uiExecuteImport) and section banners help. But it is one 3.5k-line file of long template-string HTML with inline handlers, and the allocation/tail-difference logic has almost no comments.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: One new 3502-line file, which caps this at accept. The UI copies business logic: updateAfterSalePreview re-implements refund allocation and the all-refunded check, and refundedBySku is built twice in the modal code. Handlers are attached as window.* globals.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Inputs are validated (Number.isInteger qty, phone regex) and import failures are reported. Money is float math with round2 (round2(order.payable - order.refundedAmount)). Hidden tests failed test_seed_products_and_orders and test_cart_rejects_out_of_stock_and_over_stock.

C9-01-CASE1.evidence: Shows subtotal/payable/refunded, a rules banner, status badges, a refund preview and toasts with readable reasons. submitAfterSaleModal calls requestAfterSale and uiExecuteImport imports without any confirm step, so refund and import overwrite have no confirmation.

C9-01-CASE2.evidence: The UI calls shopTestAPI.* for mutations and stats look derived from records. Money is float with round2 rather than integer cents, and the after-sale preview duplicates the allocation formula instead of reusing the core function.
